summary: Per-route usage widget removes tracehook links when query is executed with service-account token
description: Issue summary: Customer reports that when viewing the per-route usage widget on a saved dashboard and applying a route filter while authenticating via a service-account token, tracehook URLs shown in the widget panels vanish (links become plain text). Impact: Customers cannot jump from usage spikes to correlated traces, slowing incident response and troubleshooting. Environment: Production console, us-east, multiple orgs in dedicated cluster. Observed since 2026-03-09 08:00 UTC after a console deploy. Affects dashboards that use the per-route aggregation and where the query is proxied through the usage-aggregator with service-account identity headers.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Log into customer org UI using a service-account token (not a regular user cookie).
2) Open a saved dashboard that includes the per-route usage widget (time range: last 6h).
3) Add a filter drop-in for route.name = 'web.ingest.v2' and apply the filter.
4) Hover over a spike in the usage widget and click the tracehook link in the tooltip.
5) Observe the link is rendered as plain text (no clickable URL) and trace jump fails.
6) Repeat the same dashboard access as an interactive human session (cookie-based) — tracehook links work normally.
observed_logs: console:warn - tracehook: missing-tracehook-header when proxying request from service-account id=sa-34
usage-aggregator:info - query-rewrite applied for route aggregation; headers preserved: ['x-rw-org', 'x-rw-route']
tracehook-proxy:error - downstream render: template variable 'trace_url' evaluated to null; input headers: {x-rw-auth-type: 'service_account'}
frontend:debug - widget-tooltip: link-href attribute set to '' for panel id=panel-1172
comments: 2026-03-10 - Ethan Brooks (Support): Received initial report from FinSight support engineer. Asked for dashboard permalink and browser console screenshot.
2026-03-10 - Customer (FinSight): Provided permalink and two screenshots demonstrating link vs plain text when using service-account token. Mentioned this started after Tuesday deploy.
2026-03-10 - Priya Nair (SRE): Triage acknowledged. Assigned to me for investigation. Reproduced in prod with SA token; opening investigation notes.
2026-03-11 - Miguel Ortega (Frontend): Observed that widget renderer escapes href when request context has 'service_account' auth type. Hypothesis: extra sanitization path for non-interactive tokens.
2026-03-11 - Priya Nair (SRE): Linked internal INT-7891 for a recent change to auth context propagation. Requesting logs from usage-aggregator and tracehook-proxy teams.
2026-03-12 - Support (Ethan): Sent workaround to customer (use temporary user API token or view via service-account impersonation session). Customer accepted workaround while fix is prepared.
investigation_notes: - Reproduced in prod: when 'x-rw-auth-type' == 'service_account' the frontend renderer drops anchor hrefs for tooltips (escape path) — likely defensive to prevent SA tokens being surfaced in links.

- Recent change in PR #4123 introduced stricter templating for tracehook rendering; template now checks auth type and omits link when non-interactive to avoid leaking session callbacks (intended), but this behavior was too broad and removed links for service-account based trace navigation.

- Usage-aggregator is correctly adding 'x-rw-tracehook' header but tracehook-proxy returns trace URL; frontend receives trace_url == null only when the upstream response had meta.auth_type == 'service_account' due to a guard in tracehook-proxy.
- Unit tests did not cover the per-route widget tooltip rendering path; missed regression.
- Impact limited to service-account auth flows and saved dashboards using per-route aggregation; interactive users unaffected.
resolution_notes: Short-term workaround: Advise customers to view dashboards using an interactive user session or use impersonation (workaround provided to FinSight).

Fix implemented: Reverted the overbroad guard in tracehook-proxy and adjusted templating to allow tracehook links when auth_type is 'service_account' but the requesting org has 'allow_tracehook_service_accounts' flag set (config default true for dedicated).

Related PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/4128 - adds unit test for per-route widget tooltip and preserves header sanitation while enabling link rendering for service-account flows where safe.

Rollback/rollout notes: Hotfix rolled to prod us-east 2026-03-12 03:10 UTC with canary to 10% for 30 minutes, then full rollout. Monitoring: dashboards and tracehook link click-throughs observed for 30m post-rollout; no errors introduced.

Follow-ups: Add regression test in CI for service-account dashboard flows; add console feature flag 'allow_tracehook_service_accounts' to org config UI; open INT-7891 to track audit of auth propagation changes.
